title: Tameness of a finite separable extension of a discrete valuation ring passes to intermediate subextensions
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K and finite separable extensions M/L/K, and asserts that if M is tamely ramified with respect to A then so is L (source lines 34159-34165). The proof proceeds by the standard integral-closure argument. Let C/B/A be the integral closures of A in M/L/K and use the discussion of the finite separable extension remark without further mention (proof lines 34167-34171). Since C is a finite ring extension of B, the map Spec(C) -> Spec(B) is surjective, so for every maximal ideal m of B there is a maximal ideal m' of C lying over it (proof lines 34172-34175). By multiplicativity of ramification indices and the hypothesis, the ramification index of B_m over A is prime to the residue characteristic (proof lines 34176-34179). Since kappa(m')/kappa_A is finite separable, the same holds for kappa(m)/kappa_A (proof lines 34180-34181). The non-routine content is the use of multiplicativity of ramification indices to transfer tameness downwards along the tower, together with the corresponding descent of the separability of the residue extension.
